title: Empty-site construction with climbing material carriers

executionPolicy.custodyRelease: Receiving restraint and full required connection/stage acceptance must be confirmed before the sender releases; delivery, fastening, verification and carrier release form an overlapping transaction.
executionPolicy.bootstrap: Mobile robots arrive assembled, charged and carrying secured supplies; self-unload and deploy tools, foundations, first stable frame, climbing interfaces and mobile service without pre-existing site plant or people.
executionPolicy.initialSite: Empty flat terrain and declared ground/environment conditions; no installed foundations, frame, plant, rails, racks or service docks.
executionPolicy.preferredMaterialRoute: Arriving ground carriers and payload-carrying climbing robots hand components to construction robots on the growing frame.
executionPolicy.optionalLiftingEquipment: If a lift, hoist or crane is selected, its delivery, support, robotic assembly, inspection, use/extension, dismantling and departure become mandatory visible tasks for that run. It must not depend on itself to erect its first support.
executionPolicy.demonstrationPriority: Develop the continuous empty-site-to-completed-building execution alongside physical action evidence. Isolated joint benchmarks are supporting work, not the primary deliverable.

ledger.scope: Software custody, qualification and mass-balance logic; fixture inputs are synthetic, not physical inspection.

climb.scope: One unloaded local 3.6 m climb; ideal point clamps, rigid rails and disabled limb/rail collisions.

climb-failure.scope: One unreachable receiver is rejected; grip returns to its prior receiver; supported aborted climb only.

placement.scope: Prescribed crane carrier with free beam, tension-only slings and measured two-seat release; no autonomous crane.

placement-failure.scope: Missed-seat case retains crane support and inhibits approach.

fastener.scope: Modified isolated mounted tool inserts free pin, withdraws and retains 2 kN axial proof load; completeConstructionFasteningCertified=false.

connector.scope: Pin pullout challenge against deployed dogs; no robotic release or reverse assembly.

structure.scope: Independent partial-height elastic equilibrium snapshots with fixed foundations and assumed joints/braces; no capacity acceptance.

planning.scope: Analytical task-count/throughput arithmetic; no whole-building dynamics or autonomous scheduling execution.

tasks.name: Offsite fabrication and qualification
tasks.machine: Automated fabrication and inspection cell
tasks.loadCustody: Fixtures retain parts until robot inspection accepts identity and geometry
tasks.failureHold: Keep the workpiece clamped in its manufacturing fixture and quarantine its passport; do not load the delivery carrier.
tasks.acceptanceGate: Accept asset identity, geometry, condition and traceable process evidence before delivery; reject failed qualification.
tasks.statusDetail: Planned; material ledger tests use synthetic inspection inputs
requiredEvidence: applicable power-loss, capture, sensing and communication failure runs

tasks.name: Robot fleet arrival and incoming transport
tasks.machine: Self-propelled ground robots and driverless material carriers
tasks.loadCustody: Deck restraints remain engaged through arrival
tasks.failureHold: Brake at a validated stopping location while deck restraints remain mechanically locked; request only an automated route/recovery action.
tasks.acceptanceGate: Show the fleet and secured cargo entering the initially empty site; complete the declared driverless route and stopping/cargo-restraint checks.
tasks.statusDetail: Planned; no complete fleet arrival or transport simulation
requiredEvidence: applicable power-loss, capture, sensing and communication failure runs

tasks.name: Arrival, parking and cargo registration
tasks.machine: Arriving robots, onboard scanner and carrier controller
tasks.loadCustody: Vehicle restraints retain cargo while robots establish parking and bootstrap work zones
tasks.failureHold: Keep vehicle cargo restraints locked and inhibit unloading until dock and identity discrepancies resolve.
tasks.acceptanceGate: Agree asset identities, cargo restraints and parking positions before self-unloading; no prebuilt yard or dock is assumed.
tasks.statusDetail: Planned; software passport logic is partial evidence only
requiredEvidence: applicable power-loss, capture, sensing and communication failure runs

tasks.name: Bootstrap self-unloading and subsequent cargo unloading
tasks.machine: Self-unloading carriers and arriving mobile manipulators
tasks.loadCustody: Cargo restraint and gripper overlap until measured gripper custody
tasks.failureHold: Keep carrier restraints locked when capture fails; after partial pickup establish carrier or independent rack support before releasing the manipulator.
tasks.acceptanceGate: Unload the first tools and supplies using the arriving fleet itself. Establish measured gripper/support custody before releasing cargo restraints; no erected gantry or crane is a prerequisite.
tasks.statusDetail: Planned; no unloading simulation
requiredEvidence: applicable power-loss, capture, sensing and communication failure runs

tasks.name: Bootstrap equipment deployment
tasks.machine: Self-deploying mobile manipulators and ground robots
tasks.loadCustody: Transport/deployment fixtures retain tools, temporary supports and equipment until deployed restraints pass
tasks.failureHold: Retain transport or independent deployment restraints; do not use incompletely deployed equipment.
tasks.acceptanceGate: Deploy the selected ground machines, fixtures and storage supports from incoming cargo. Any optional lifting plant requires its own visible support, assembly, inspection and eventual removal sequence.
tasks.statusDetail: Planned; self-deployment and conditional lifting-equipment assembly are absent
requiredEvidence: applicable power-loss, capture, sensing and communication failure runs

tasks.name: Ground survey and access preparation
tasks.machine: Survey rover and earthmoving fleet
tasks.loadCustody: Ground equipment keeps tools and spoil in controlled zones
tasks.failureHold: Park ground equipment with tools secured, retain supported excavations and inhibit foundations when bearing, map or survey evidence fails.
tasks.acceptanceGate: Use visibly arrived and unloaded survey/ground equipment; confirm geometry, access, bearing assumptions and ground preparation before foundation work.
tasks.statusDetail: Planned; no terrain or geotechnical model
requiredEvidence: applicable power-loss, capture, sensing and communication failure runs

tasks.name: Foundations and anchors
tasks.machine: Arriving foundation rig and mobile ground manipulator
tasks.loadCustody: Rig or fixtures retain components until foundation acceptance
tasks.failureHold: Keep foundation components supported by deployed ground equipment; retain incomplete excavation support and inhibit frame loading.
tasks.acceptanceGate: Visibly install the selected foundation/base system and verify its stated ground/load assumptions. Its supplies and tooling must have arrived and been unloaded.
tasks.statusDetail: Planned; tower analysis assumes fixed bases
requiredEvidence: applicable power-loss, capture, sensing and communication failure runs

tasks.name: Charging and service infrastructure setup
tasks.machine: Mobile service robot
tasks.loadCustody: Ground supports retain docks and supplies until connections pass
tasks.failureHold: Keep service equipment on ground restraints, isolate supply interfaces and inhibit use of an unaccepted dock.
tasks.acceptanceGate: Arriving machines use declared bootstrap reserves to deploy mobile service; accept restraints and supply interfaces before recurring missions exceed those reserves.
tasks.statusDetail: Planned; no energy or charging model
requiredEvidence: applicable power-loss, capture, sensing and communication failure runs

tasks.name: Yard storage and allocation
tasks.machine: Yard carrier and rack robot
tasks.loadCustody: Rack and manipulator overlap custody
tasks.failureHold: Retain the accepted rack/gripper restraint and quarantine the asset on identity or stability failure; do not allocate it.
tasks.acceptanceGate: Confirm rack stability and identity; reserve only qualified assets and prove physical retrieval.
tasks.statusDetail: Planned; allocation software does not establish physical storage
requiredEvidence: applicable power-loss, capture, sensing and communication failure runs

tasks.name: Payload attachment and carrier pickup
tasks.machine: Ground or climbing carrier, handling robot and payload cradle
tasks.loadCustody: Rack or transport support overlaps with a mechanically engaged carrier restraint
tasks.failureHold: Retain rack/transport support if the cradle or grip fails; inhibit climb until load restraint and payload limits pass.
tasks.acceptanceGate: Retrieve an identified component, mechanically secure it to its carrier, verify payload and center of mass, and reserve its usable ground or climbing route. First-frame deliveries use ground routes and do not require an existing frame. If lifting rigging is selected, robots must attach and verify it visibly.
tasks.statusDetail: Planned; no loaded carrier pickup or payload-restraint simulation
requiredEvidence: applicable power-loss, capture, sensing and communication failure runs

tasks.name: First stable frame and progressive climbing interfaces
tasks.machine: Ground assembly manipulators, then frame-mounted construction robots
tasks.loadCustody: Ground manipulators or existing accepted structure support new members, braces and climbing interfaces
tasks.failureHold: Retain payload and temporary fixtures; prohibit mounting or extending from unaccepted structure and preserve ground or return access.
tasks.acceptanceGate: Build the first stable bay within ground reach. Then deliver and install each additional rail/receiver or integrated interface from already accepted structure before a climber uses it.
tasks.statusDetail: Planned; existing climb fixtures begin already installed
requiredEvidence: applicable power-loss, capture, sensing and communication failure runs

tasks.name: Robot deployment, loaded ascent and work-position travel
tasks.machine: Climbing material carriers, construction robots and any coupled carrier team
tasks.loadCustody: Accepted frame grips retain each robot; payload cradle or tool restraint retains its carried cargo
tasks.failureHold: Retain the continuing accepted supports; reject failed capture and use an independently validated return or recovery restraint. No additional grip releases after an unresolved failure.
tasks.acceptanceGate: Show each carrier and assembler attaching from the ground, ascending and reaching its reserved work position. Verify payload/tool-specific finite grips, actuator limits, clearance, return capacity and continuous support. Receiving assemblers must be present and ready before a delivery starts.
tasks.statusDetail: Planned loaded transport; existing partial evidence is only an unloaded local 3.6 m climb with ideal clamps
requiredEvidence: applicable power-loss, capture, sensing and communication failure runs

tasks.name: Material delivery and supported placement
tasks.machine: Climbing carriers and frame-mounted construction robots
tasks.loadCustody: Carrier and receiving assembler/fixture overlap custody; carrier remains attached through fastening and verification
tasks.failureHold: Keep the component on accepted carrier and receiving supports; wait, return or enter a supported abort on failed rendezvous, capture or seating.
tasks.acceptanceGate: Reach a reserved delivery position with the receiving assembler already deployed and ready; establish receiving capture, orient and seat the component while retaining sending support. Do not release the carrier at the end of this task.
tasks.statusDetail: Planned; earlier prescribed-hoist seating is background evidence, not loaded climbing delivery
requiredEvidence: applicable power-loss, capture, sensing and communication failure runs

tasks.name: Structural fastening
tasks.machine: Construction robot with reversible connection tooling
tasks.loadCustody: Carrier, assembler, seats and temporary restraints retain the member throughout fastening
tasks.failureHold: Retain carrier/assembler and temporary restraint support if insertion, latching or connection verification fails.
tasks.acceptanceGate: Complete the engineered connections with reachable tooling and verified engagement. Carry support forward to structural-stage acceptance; no timed custody release.
tasks.statusDetail: Partial isolated simulation: modified mounted pusher/free pin retains a 2 kN axial proof load; complete building connection absent
requiredEvidence: applicable power-loss, capture, sensing and communication failure runs

tasks.name: Bracing and structural stage acceptance
tasks.machine: Brace installers and inspection rover
tasks.loadCustody: Temporary bracing stays until replacement load path passes
tasks.failureHold: Retain carrier and temporary supports; halt additional loading until brace, joint and stage acceptance passes.
tasks.acceptanceGate: Install required bracing and accept the current structural stage including simultaneous robots and payloads before carrier release, new ascent or further loading. Bootstrap bracing is established within A11.
tasks.statusDetail: Analytical and software evidence only; no robotic brace installation
requiredEvidence: applicable power-loss, capture, sensing and communication failure runs

tasks.name: Carrier release, return and next mission
tasks.machine: Climbing material carrier or coupled carrier team
tasks.loadCustody: Accepted structural connection retains the installed part before carrier restraints open; frame grips retain the departing robot
tasks.failureHold: Keep payload restraint if final transfer fails; wait on accepted grips if the return route is blocked, and reserve a supported recovery route.
tasks.acceptanceGate: Confirm installation and stage acceptance, visibly release the carrier, traverse and descend or route to the next supply task, and return the same robot identity without teleportation.
tasks.statusDetail: Planned; no loaded delivery followed by accepted installation and empty return is simulated
requiredEvidence: blocked return, failed release and energy-reserve failure runs

tasks.name: Floors, core, circulation and roof installation
tasks.machine: Component-specific climbing carriers and construction robots; optional assembled lifting plant only if selected
tasks.loadCustody: Carriers, assemblers and temporary supports retain modules until all required connections pass
tasks.failureHold: Retain payload restraint and temporary catches; return or secure failed floor, roof, core or stair modules.
tasks.acceptanceGate: Deliver and install the specified floors, circulation/core and roof through the same pickup, carry, handoff, connection and stage-acceptance transaction. Do not assume existing heavy panels are climbable payloads.
tasks.statusDetail: Planned; geometry and catalogue arithmetic do not demonstrate installation
requiredEvidence: applicable power-loss, capture, sensing and communication failure runs

tasks.name: Facade, terraces and weather closure
tasks.machine: Facade handling and seal robots
tasks.loadCustody: Mechanical grippers and temporary catches retain panels until attachments pass
tasks.failureHold: Retain panel gripper and mechanical catches; return to an accepted storage support on attachment failure and quarantine seal failures.
tasks.acceptanceGate: Deliver and attach facade, glazing and terrace modules with weather closures; preserve remaining material routes and robot escape access before closing each area.
tasks.statusDetail: Planned; no facade manipulation, attachment or seal test
requiredEvidence: applicable power-loss, capture, sensing and communication failure runs

tasks.name: Services and interior modules
tasks.machine: Service module and connection robots
tasks.loadCustody: Fixtures retain modules until mechanical and utility acceptance
tasks.failureHold: Keep modules supported and utilities isolated; lock out downstream commissioning on failed or conflicting connection tests.
tasks.acceptanceGate: Accept mechanical connections, utility isolation and required pressure/electrical/fire tests before energizing services.
tasks.statusDetail: Planned; electrical, fluid and fire performance unmodeled
requiredEvidence: applicable power-loss, capture, sensing and communication failure runs

tasks.name: Staged inspection and commissioning
tasks.machine: Inspection robots and test equipment
tasks.loadCustody: Accepted supports retain components; unaccepted systems remain isolated and occupancy stays prohibited
tasks.failureHold: Keep occupancy prohibited and preserve temporary supports; isolate failed utilities and quarantine incomplete acceptance records.
tasks.acceptanceGate: Inspect the installed building inventory, including roof and specified systems; reject missing or stale acceptance. Repeat affected checks after later closures or temporary-support removal. Final closure and site-finish acceptance occur within A22 before final departure; appearance alone is not commissioning.
tasks.statusDetail: Planned; prototype result files are not autonomous inspection evidence
requiredEvidence: applicable power-loss, capture, sensing and communication failure runs

tasks.name: Charging and tool exchange
tasks.machine: Docking climber and service robot
tasks.loadCustody: Independent dock restraint holds robot
tasks.failureHold: Keep independent docking restraints engaged; retain the previous tool or catch the replacement mechanically; isolate charging and prohibit mission start on insufficient reserve.
tasks.acceptanceGate: Establish independent dock custody, latch overlap and isolation before tool release or charging; retain mission/recovery energy reserve.
tasks.statusDetail: Planned; batteries, electrical energy and tool latches absent
requiredEvidence: applicable power-loss, capture, sensing and communication failure runs

tasks.name: Fault recovery
tasks.machine: Redundant recovery robot and supervisory controller
tasks.loadCustody: Backup support establishes custody before disturbing failed machine
tasks.failureHold: Establish redundant mechanical custody before touching a failed machine; if recovery cannot pass, maintain a supported abort without continuing work.
tasks.acceptanceGate: Inject declared faults; establish backup mechanical custody and complete automated recovery or a mechanically supported abort without human intervention.
tasks.statusDetail: Partial local simulation only for returning one missed grip to its previous receiver
requiredEvidence: applicable power-loss, capture, sensing and communication failure runs

tasks.name: Temporary-work recovery, site finish and fleet departure
tasks.machine: Descending climbers, inspection and ground recovery robots, and service carriers
tasks.loadCustody: Accepted structure, docks and carriers retain every machine and removed temporary component through cleanup
tasks.failureHold: Keep necessary supports and escape routes until all dependent machines depart; suspend equipment recovery on unresolved custody.
tasks.acceptanceGate: Show permitted brace/rail removal, robot descent, final facade/access closure, ground finish/planting and optional lifting-equipment dismantling. Inspect those final works and changed support states before accepting completion. Then pack remaining tools, inspection/service equipment and show the final ground machine driving away.
tasks.statusDetail: Planned; complete cleanup, descent and last-machine departure are absent
requiredEvidence: applicable power-loss, capture, sensing and communication failure runs

tasks.name: Deconstruction survey and support setup
tasks.machine: Inspection and temporary support robots
tasks.loadCustody: Existing structure remains until accepted shoring and removal plan
tasks.failureHold: Keep the existing structure and utilities in their current accepted state until survey, isolation and shoring acceptance; prohibit connection release.
tasks.acceptanceGate: Begin a later recovery mission with visibly arriving machines, condition survey, isolation and accepted shoring before releasing any existing load path. Construction departure does not itself dismantle the building.
tasks.statusDetail: Planned; static stage analyses are not reverse-construction history
requiredEvidence: applicable power-loss, capture, sensing and communication failure runs

tasks.name: Service disconnection and enclosure removal
tasks.machine: Service isolation and panel removal robots
tasks.loadCustody: Verify isolation and receiving gripper custody before disconnecting
tasks.failureHold: Keep attachment/gripper restraint overlap and utility isolation; leave a panel/module supported when isolation or receiving custody cannot be confirmed.
tasks.acceptanceGate: Verify utilities isolated and draining/energy discharge complete; establish receiving custody before any panel/service disconnect.
tasks.statusDetail: Planned; no reverse services or facade operation
requiredEvidence: applicable power-loss, capture, sensing and communication failure runs

tasks.name: Reverse structural release
tasks.machine: Connection release robots, material carriers and shoring robots
tasks.loadCustody: Carrier/assembler and shoring take the measured member load before unlatching
tasks.failureHold: Keep original connections engaged until receiving load pickup is accepted; after partial release retain redundant support and inhibit neighboring removal.
tasks.acceptanceGate: Establish measured receiving support, actuate reversible connections, extract and carry the member away without destabilizing the residual structure. Optional lifting equipment must already have its own accepted setup.
tasks.statusDetail: Planned; pin pullout challenge does not demonstrate robotic unlatching and removal
requiredEvidence: applicable power-loss, capture, sensing and communication failure runs

tasks.name: Recovery sorting and inspection
tasks.machine: Yard handling and inspection cell
tasks.loadCustody: Identified racks keep recovered components
tasks.failureHold: Keep parts in identified quarantine racks; issue no reuse qualification when condition, identity or lineage is uncertain.
tasks.acceptanceGate: Identify, measure and inspect recovered parts; quarantine uncertainty before issuing a new qualification record.
tasks.statusDetail: Software evidence only; physical inspection and qualification absent
requiredEvidence: applicable power-loss, capture, sensing and communication failure runs

tasks.name: Repair reuse and recycling
tasks.machine: Repair/refabrication cell and driverless carrier
tasks.loadCustody: Fixtures retain material through repair
tasks.failureHold: Keep material in repair/refabrication fixtures or quarantine stock; reject reuse allocation and prevent a ledger completion on unmeasured yield or failed inspection.
tasks.acceptanceGate: Validate real repair and inspection processes; preserve identity on direct reuse and record new lineage, mass losses and process evidence on recycling.
tasks.statusDetail: Software evidence only; yields, energy and inspection fixtures are assumed
requiredEvidence: applicable power-loss, capture, sensing and communication failure runs

tasks.name: Final plant and foundation recovery
tasks.machine: Dismantling machines and mobile recovery carrier
tasks.loadCustody: Last independent mobile carrier retains departing plant
tasks.failureHold: Keep remaining anchors and deployment supports needed by plant; secure removed parts on an independent carrier and halt last-machine departure when custody is unresolved.
tasks.acceptanceGate: Prove foundation/anchor removability, sequencing and last-machine recovery; retain supports needed by remaining equipment.
tasks.statusDetail: Planned; foundation recovery method depends on engineered design
requiredEvidence: applicable power-loss, capture, sensing and communication failure runs

notes: Task IDs are stable identifiers, not chronological numbering. This graph is a proposed task-type dependency graph, not simulated timing.
A11 first-frame work uses ground reach. Repeated A11 instances extend interfaces from accepted prior structure; later-stage climbs depend on those specific instances and the prior A15 acceptance.
A13 delivery, A14 fastening, A15 stage acceptance and A29 release/return form one continuous custody transaction. The carrier does not release at seating alone.
A16-A18 module operations instantiate component-specific pickup, carrier delivery, fastening, acceptance and return transactions; the aggregate graph does not substitute for them.
A20 service and A21 recovery are ongoing readiness requirements, including bootstrap reserves; they are not guaranteed by graph acyclicity.
Any selected lift, hoist or crane expands A06 into explicit delivery/support/robot-assembly/inspection tasks and A22 into dismantling/removal tasks; no such equipment is mandatory by default.
Construction completion and later regenerative deconstruction have distinct scopes. A01 is qualified upstream supply at the visible arrival boundary.
No existing evidence makes the entire new route physically verified. Unloaded climb evidence does not establish payload capacity or loaded handoff.
Climb motor work is not electrical/battery energy. A single missed-grip recovery does not establish general fault tolerance.
A12 includes deployment and repositioning of receiving construction robots, not just carriers. Repeated A11 interface work requires those robots to have reached supported work positions.

A19 inspections occur by installed stage. A22 includes renewed inspection of final closures, support removals and ground finish before final acceptance and departure; earlier commissioning cannot accept parts not yet installed.

construction.finalState: Declared building complete, temporary works recovered, all robots and construction equipment departed.

laterRegenerativeLifecycle.prerequisite: Completed construction and a new inspection/recovery mission
laterRegenerativeLifecycle.finalState: Supported dismantling, inspection, qualified reuse or recorded processing losses, recovered plant and declared site residuals.

completionScopes.meaning: Each scope requires all instantiated tasks and interfaces, including any selected lifting-equipment branch. Planning completion is distinct from verified physical execution.
